 MCC releases NEET PG 2026 Round 2 provisional seat allotment result on mcc.nic.in. Final result follows next day. MD, MS, DNB, PG Diploma seats across AIQ and deemed universities allocated.
 MedAdmit News Desk · 16 Nov 2026 · 4 min read The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has released the provisional seat allotment result for Round 2 of NEET PG 2026 counselling. Candidates can now check their allotment status on the official MCC portal using their login credentials or rank number. The final seat allotment result will be announced the following day. This round covers MD, MS, DNB, and PG Diploma courses across All India Quota (AIQ) seats, deemed universities, central universities, and other participating medical colleges.
 Check your provisional Round 2 seat allotment on mcc.nic.in today; the final result will be released tomorrow, so verify your status and prepare for the next steps in counselling.

 Unlock My College List When and Where to Check Your Provisional Allotment
 The provisional seat allotment result for NEET PG 2026 Round 2 has been made available on the official MCC website at mcc.nic.in. Every candidate who participated in Round 2 counselling can now log in using their credentials or NEET PG rank to view their allotment status.
 The portal allows you to see which course, college, and speciality (if any) has been provisionally assigned to you. This is not your final allotment—it is a preliminary result that gives you 24 hours to review and prepare for the final announcement.
 What Courses and Colleges Are Included in Round 2
 Round 2 of NEET PG 2026 counselling allocates seats across four main postgraduate pathways: MD (Doctor of Medicine), MS (Master of Surgery), DNB (Diplomate of National Board), and PG Diploma courses. These seats span multiple categories of institutions.
 Seats are available under the All India Quota (AIQ), which ensures pan-India competition and mobility. Additionally, Round 2 includes seats from deemed universities, central universities, and other medical colleges that participate in the MCC counselling process. This broad coverage means candidates have access to a diverse range of colleges and specialities across the country.
 MD courses (e.g., Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, Pathology, Microbiology, Pharmacology, Forensic Medicine, Radiology, Anaesthesia, Community Medicine) 
 MS courses (e.g., General Surgery, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Orthopaedics, Ophthalmology, ENT, Urology) 
 DNB broad-speciality courses (equivalent to MD/MS, run by NBEMS) 
 PG Diploma courses (shorter, 2-year postgraduate qualifications in select specialities) 
 Seats in deemed universities, central universities, and state medical colleges 
 Understanding Provisional vs. Final Allotment
 A provisional allotment is a temporary seat assignment released before the final result. It serves two purposes: it allows candidates to see their likely placement and gives them time to raise objections or clarifications if they believe there is an error in the allotment process.
 Know the exact MD/MS/DNB seats your rank can get

 See My Colleges The final seat allotment result will be announced on the day following the provisional release. Once the final result is declared, the provisional allotment becomes binding (unless you have successfully challenged it or opted for a higher round). It is therefore critical to review your provisional allotment carefully and report any discrepancies immediately to MCC.
 What to Do After Checking Your Provisional Result
 After logging in and viewing your provisional allotment, take the following steps. First, verify that your personal details, NEET PG rank, and category are correct. Second, check whether the course and college assigned match your preferences and eligibility. Third, if you spot any error—such as a wrong rank, category, or course code—note it down and prepare to lodge a formal complaint with MCC before the final result is announced.
 If your allotment is satisfactory, you do not need to take any action at this stage. Simply wait for the final result. If you are not satisfied with your allotment or believe an error has occurred, contact MCC's help desk or use the official portal's grievance mechanism to file a complaint. MCC typically provides a window of a few hours between the provisional and final result for candidates to raise objections.
 Verify your name, rank, category, and NEET PG score on the allotment letter 
 Check the course code, speciality name, and college name assigned to you 
 Compare the allotment with your preference list to ensure it aligns with your choices 
 If an error is found, take a screenshot and file a complaint with MCC immediately 
 Do not ignore the provisional result; use it as a preview to prepare for the final outcome 
 What Happens After the Final Result Is Announced
 Once the final seat allotment result is released, it becomes official and binding. Candidates who have been allotted a seat must then proceed to the next phase of counselling, which typically involves reporting to the allotted college, completing document verification, and paying the admission fee within a specified deadline.
 Failure to report or pay the fee within the deadline may result in forfeiture of your seat, and it may be offered to the next candidate in the merit list. Therefore, mark the final result date on your calendar and be ready to act quickly once it is announced. Keep all your original documents (MBBS degree, NEET PG admit card, rank card, category certificate, etc.) ready for verification at the college.
 Final result is binding and non-negotiable (unless successfully challenged before declaration) 
 Candidates must report to the allotted college within the specified deadline 
 Document verification and fee payment are mandatory to confirm your seat 
 Missing the deadline may lead to cancellation of your allotment 
 If you do not accept the allotment, you may be eligible for a higher round (if available)

 See My Colleges To check your provisional allotment, visit mcc.nic.in and navigate to the NEET PG counselling section. You will be prompted to log in using your NEET PG registration number and password, or alternatively, your rank number and date of birth. Ensure you use the correct credentials; if you have forgotten your password, use the 'Forgot Password' option to reset it.
 If you encounter technical issues such as a slow-loading page, error messages, or inability to log in, try the following: clear your browser cache and cookies, use a different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), disable any VPN or proxy, or try accessing the site from a different device. If the problem persists, contact MCC's technical support team via the helpline number or email provided on the website. Do not wait until the last moment to check your result; log in early to avoid server congestion.
 Use your NEET PG registration number and password to log in 
 Alternatively, use your rank number and date of birth 
 Clear browser cache if the page does not load 
 Try a different browser or device if you face technical issues 
 Contact MCC support if you cannot access the portal 
 Check your result well before the final announcement to avoid last-minute rush 
 Key Dates and Timeline for NEET PG 2026 Round 2
 The provisional seat allotment result for Round 2 was released on 16 November 2026. The final seat allotment result is scheduled to be announced on 17 November 2026. Between these two dates, candidates have a narrow window to review their provisional allotment and raise any objections or clarifications with MCC.
 After the final result is declared, the timeline for reporting to colleges, document verification, and fee payment will be communicated by MCC. Typically, candidates are given 3–5 days to report and complete these formalities. Mark these dates in your calendar and ensure you do not miss any deadline, as delays can result in loss of your seat.
 Provisional result: 16 November 2026 
 Final result: 17 November 2026 
 Objection window: Between provisional and final result (typically a few hours) 
 Reporting and document verification: Dates to be announced by MCC (usually 3–5 days after final result) 
 Fee payment deadline: To be announced by MCC 
 What If You Are Not Satisfied With Your Allotment
 If your provisional allotment does not match your expectations or preferences, you have limited options. First, check whether an error has been made in the allotment process (e.g., wrong rank, category, or course code). If an error is confirmed, file a complaint with MCC immediately. Second, if the allotment is correct but you are unhappy with the course or college, you may choose to participate in a higher round of counselling (if available) by forfeiting your current seat.
 However, forfeiting a seat in Round 2 means you will re-enter the merit list for Round 3 or subsequent rounds, and there is no guarantee you will receive a better allotment. Weigh this decision carefully. Some candidates choose to accept their Round 2 allotment and join, while others prefer to wait for a higher round. Consult with your mentors, seniors, or counsellors before making this decision.
 Verify that no error has been made in your allotment 
 If an error exists, file a complaint with MCC before the final result 
 If you are unhappy with the allotment, you may forfeit and participate in a higher round 
 Forfeiting a seat carries the risk of not getting a better allotment in the next round 
 Seek advice from seniors or mentors before deciding to forfeit

 When was the NEET PG 2026 Round 2 provisional seat allotment result released?
 The provisional seat allotment result for NEET PG 2026 Round 2 was released on 16 November 2026. Candidates can check their allotment status on mcc.nic.in using their login credentials or rank number.
 What is the difference between provisional and final seat allotment in NEET PG counselling?
 A provisional allotment is a temporary, preliminary result released first to allow candidates to review and raise objections if needed. The final allotment is the official, binding result announced the next day (17 November 2026 in this case). Once the final result is declared, it becomes non-negotiable unless successfully challenged before the announcement.
 Which courses and colleges are included in NEET PG 2026 Round 2 counselling?
 Round 2 includes MD, MS, DNB, and PG Diploma courses across All India Quota (AIQ) seats, deemed universities, central universities, and other participating medical colleges. This ensures a broad range of specialities and institutions are available for allocation.
 What should I do if I find an error in my provisional seat allotment?
 If you spot an error such as a wrong rank, category, or course code, take a screenshot as evidence and file a formal complaint with MCC immediately. Use the grievance mechanism on mcc.nic.in or contact MCC's help desk. You must report the error before the final result is announced to have it corrected.
 What happens after the final seat allotment result is announced?
 After the final result is declared, you must report to your allotted college within the specified deadline (typically 3–5 days). You will need to complete document verification and pay the admission fee to confirm your seat. Failure to report or pay within the deadline may result in forfeiture of your seat.
 Can I forfeit my Round 2 allotment and participate in a higher round?
 Yes, you can choose to forfeit your Round 2 seat and participate in a higher round of counselling. However, this means you will re-enter the merit list and there is no guarantee of a better allotment. Weigh the risks carefully and seek advice from mentors before making this decision.
 How do I log in to mcc.nic.in to check my provisional allotment?
 Visit mcc.nic.in and navigate to the NEET PG counselling section. Log in using your NEET PG registration number and password, or alternatively, your rank number and date of birth. If you have forgotten your password, use the 'Forgot Password' option to reset it.
 What should I do if I cannot access mcc.nic.in or face technical issues?
 Try clearing your browser cache and cookies, using a different browser, disabling any VPN, or accessing the site from a different device. If the problem persists, contact MCC's technical support team via the helpline or email provided on the website. Check your result early to avoid server congestion closer to the deadline.
 Review your provisional allotment carefully on mcc.nic.in today and report any errors to MCC before the final result is announced tomorrow. Once the final allotment is declared, be ready to report to your college and complete document verification and fee payment within the specified deadline to secure your seat.
